text:
**For most people, I’d pick Starling as the best everyday main account.** It’s fee-free, has a well-regarded app and 24-hour support, and doesn’t charge for card spending or cash withdrawals abroad. It’s a good simple choice if you want your salary, bills and day-to-day spending in one place.

If you’re happy to manage a couple of accounts, **Chase may be better for cashback**: it currently offers 2% on eligible everyday spending—such as groceries, eating out, transport and fuel—up to £20 a month. But you’ll need to make at least 15 payments a month and keep £1,000 in a Chase savings account to qualify. Check the exclusions and terms before relying on the reward.

Other good fits:
- **Monzo** if budgeting tools and spending categories matter most.
- **Santander Edge** if you mainly want cashback on household bills paid by Direct Debit; its £3 monthly fee and eligibility conditions matter.
- **Zopa Biscuit** if you want a separate account for bills or eating out: choose 3% cashback in one of those categories, capped at £150 of qualifying spend per month.

**Bottom line:** Starling for a straightforward main account; Chase for everyday-spending cashback if you meet the conditions. Account benefits and rates can change, so check the provider’s current terms before applying.
